title: Keep special keys visible
description: Keep Ctrl, Esc, arrows, and other terminal keys within reach.

steps.title: Open the Host List menu
steps.text: From the Host List, tap the three-dot menu in the top corner.

steps.title: Open Settings
steps.text: Choose Settings. This changes ConnectBot's app-wide settings, rather than the settings for an individual host.

steps.title: Find the Keyboard section
steps.text: Scroll down to the Keyboard section. Look for Special keys always visible.

steps.title: Keep the special keys visible
steps.text: Turn on Special keys always visible. This keeps the terminal's special-key toolbar on screen

steps.title: Return to the Host List
steps.text: Go back to the Host List. Your setting is saved automatically.

steps.title: Try a terminal session
steps.text: Open a terminal session. The special keys now stay visible and doesn't overlap the terminal.

title: Add an SSH host
description: Save a server so it is ready to open from the Host List.

steps.title: Add a host
steps.text: From the Host List, tap the plus button to add a host.

steps.title: Enter the connection details
steps.text: In Quick connect, enter your username, server address, and optionally port, like demo@example.com. Remember, this is only an example host, so you must replace these example details with your own. Port 22 is the usual SSH port.
steps.spoken: In Quick connect, enter your username, server address, and optionally port. For example: demo, at, example dot com. Remember, this is only an example host, so you must replace these example details with your own. Port twenty-two is the usual SSH port.

steps.title: Save the host
steps.text: Tap Add host to save the connection.

steps.title: Find your saved host
steps.text: The saved host appears in the Host List. Simply tap it when you are ready to connect.

title: Customize terminal appearance
description: Use a profile to choose a terminal color scheme and a readable font size.

steps.title: Open the Host List menu
steps.text: From the Host List, open the three-dot menu.

steps.title: Open Profiles
steps.text: Choose Profiles. Profiles let you reuse terminal appearance settings across hosts.

steps.title: Create a profile
steps.text: Tap the plus button and name the new profile something memorable. I'll use 'Readable' in this example.

steps.title: Choose a color scheme
steps.text: Under Color Scheme, select Solarized Dark. Terminal colors are independent of the app's light or dark theme.

steps.title: Choose a font size
steps.text: Set Font Size to a font size that is comfortable on your screen.

steps.title: Save the profile
steps.text: Tap Save, then return to the Host List.

steps.title: Assign the profile to a host
steps.text: Edit the host you want to customize, choose Readable under Profile, and save the host.

steps.title: Open the terminal
steps.text: The next session for the host will use the colors and font size you chose.
